test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 28 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Bears are Teddies.

Some Rabbits are Teddies.

All Rabbits are Soft.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Rabbits are Bears.

(II) All Teddies are Soft.
solution:
According to the statements, we will get the Venn diagram as:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0cb29d3f51cfb4fff2ce6b41cb8e9687fae983c200125358ce577951ce8f1f4c.png] 

Let's check all the conclusions as:

(I) Some Rabbits are Bears → Does not follow → There is no relation given between bears and rabbits and also the Venn diagram shows no relation so the conclusion does not follow.

(II) All Teddies are Soft → Does not follow → From the given information only some rabbits are teddies which means only some teddies are soft so the conclusion does not follow.

Thus, **neither** **conclusions I nor II follow**.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**
